summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). Studio did not run: simulation status is 'skipped', simulation_allowed=false, and no artifacts were produced. The scenario is the static multi-source 9x9 mm eQFN case in Section 4.4 (Figure 13, Table 1) of the TRIC paper, extracted as a custom_2d_steady experiment with an empty floorplan and empty power_w. The gate blocked it because a custom experiment needs 1-128 blocks and a power_w object. Further blockers include a missing cited observable and regime in the gate record, unresolved adversarial checks, and a pending independent page/asset review. Because this is a custom 2D steady run, there is no transient trace. It is not a bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, and no Ascend910 or ATPlace pinned sizes/powers were supplied, so no input.flp or one-row input.ptrace was generated and no source commit or generated-placement assumption applies. No paper-linked assets or pinned commits exist. The paper's published inputs are the 4x4 mm die, four 1x1 mm sources, and 0.5 W each (2 W total). Heat-source coordinates exist only in the Figure 13 sketch and were not digitized. The reference observable is the Layout #1 die-maximum steady temperature rise of 57.06 K over ambient (TRIC; the paper says it agrees with FloTHERM within 3%, but the FloTHERM maps are not shown). No Studio temperature exists, so no numerical comparison is made and comparison_valid=false. Even if a Studio run were later made, the location, aggregation, regime and boundary assumptions would not match: the paper uses a 3D molded-package compact model with unstated ambient and boundary conditions for this case, while Studio would use a 2D placement with its own package, materials and cooling. Only qualitative sensitivity discussion (for example, that source layout and spacing affect the die maximum) would be defensible. No exact replication is claimed and the final verdict is not_2d_applicable.

The original model is a 3D detailed thermal model of a molded eQFN package (die, die attach, epad, pins, mold, board). A 2D chip-level Studio placement cannot reproduce the vertical heat paths through the die attach, epad and board.

The paper uses JEDEC-style boundary conditions for the junction-to-ambient environment, with a board modelled as one parallelepiped of adjusted conductivity and pins as a homogenised block. Section 4.4 does not state the ambient or cooling boundary conditions for this case, so Studio cooling cannot be matched.

The solver differs. The paper uses a parametric projection-based compact model validated against FloTHERM finite-volume results, while Studio uses its own solver, so numerical results are not directly comparable.
The eQFN package has no interposer or 3D stacking, so those mismatches are not applicable, but the package-level geometry is not equivalent to a chiplet or interposer layout.

The paper has no optimizer, controller, reliability analysis or transient behaviour in this scenario (static case). Studio's optimizer or controller features therefore have no counterpart in the original setup.

No complete paper-derived floorplan can be built because the heat-source positions are available only in a figure sketch. Any Studio run would use a separate, illustrative 2D placement whose coordinates are generated by the runner and are not paper facts.

If an illustrative case is built, the published dimensions are the 4 x 4 mm2 die and four 1 x 1 mm2 sources, with 0.5 W each (2 W total, stated explicitly in the paper). No power is split by an unpublished rule.

Studio's bundled package and material assumptions would replace the paper's STMicroelectronics eQFN materials, pin and board homogenisation, and JEDEC boundary conditions. Temperatures from such a run must not be compared numerically with Table 1.
